title: Cross-mode escalation bridge and staged fix for cascading 5xx/timeouts
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers escalated intermittent 5xx and end-to-end timeouts across Hosted and Dedicated endpoints; Private customers reported similar failures during a maintenance window. We believe a combination of (1) proxy-level connection backpressure, (2) KV cache eviction thrashing, and (3) naive client retry amplification led to request storms and cascading 5xx responses. This ticket tracks a staged mitigation and durable fix that spans hosted, dedicated, and private routing layers, plus an operational runbook for escalations.
reproduction_steps: 1) Replay tenant workload observed in production (synthetic runner) at 2x normal QPS while toggling KV compaction.
hypothesis: Root cause is cascading resource exhaustion triggered by synchronous upstream hedged retries and edge proxy queuing. Long-lived streaming and multipart uploads increase connection counts which starve keepalive pools; combined with aggressive client retries this produces transient 502/504 waves. Dedicated pools experience the same failure mode when autoscaler briefly fails to bring up warm nodes.
short_term_mitigations:
- Deploy proxy hotpatch to fast-fail requests with >120s server timeouts and return structured guidance to SDKs.
- Reduce SDK default retry multiplier for affected tenants to 1.
- Temporarily widen circuit-breaker thresholds for priority tenants to avoid unnecessary failovers.
- Enable tenant-specific admission control: shed <5% of low-priority traffic to relieve hot nodes.
- Activate async fallback queue for large multipart uploads (store-and-forward to S3-backed queue).
long_term_plan:
- Implement cross-mode escalation bridge that can route traffic away from overloaded Hosted pools to Dedicated safe-fallthrough or Private mirrors under operator control.
- Harden KV cache compaction to use staged eviction and avoid global pauses.
- Add idempotency-token window extension to prevent duplicate processing on retries.
- Improve load-aware hedging: dynamic hedging only when inflight < threshold.
- Validate autoscaler warm-start improvements for Dedicated pools.
rollout_plan: 1) Hotpatch to edge proxy (canary 2 nodes) -> monitor 30m. 2) Expand to region canary (5% traffic) with telemetry thresholds: 5xx rate, inflight sockets, retry amplification ratio. 3) Release async fallback and SDK guidance to opt-in tenants. 4) Ship KV compaction change in runtime-1.23 and coordinate Dedicated deployment during low-traffic window.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Dashboards/queries: 
- hosted/5xx_rate by tenant (alert if >0.5% increase over baseline)
- proxy/inflight_sockets (p95 and p99)
- retry_amplification_ratio = client-retries / original-requests
- kvcache/compaction_pause_ms
Runbook thresholds: 
- SLO breach: p95 latency > 3x baseline or sustained 5xx spike for 5 minutes -> page oncall.
- If inflight sockets > 80% capacity, enable tenant-shed and trigger emergency routing.
runbook: Oncall steps: 1) Identify top-5 tenants by error increase. 2) Apply per-tenant slow-path routing to Dedicated fallback pool. 3) Toggle proxy fast-fail toggle for >120s requests. 4) If situation persists, enable global soft-throttle (10%) and notify SE/CS teams with customer list. 5) After stabilization, collect traces, save pcap, and escalate to runtime team for postmortem.
